images.description: A Scout standing confidently with an emergency kit and first aid supplies, ready to respond to an emergency
Four panels showing different types of emergencies: a tornado in the distance, a house fire, a power outage with a dark neighborhood, and a first aid situation on a trail
A circular diagram showing the five aspects of emergency preparedness in a cycle: Prevention, Protection, Mitigation, Response, Recovery — with icons for each
Volunteers working together to clean up a neighborhood after a storm, stacking debris and helping neighbors carry belongings
A Scout sitting at a table filling in a chart with emergency scenarios listed in rows and the five aspects of emergency preparedness as column headers
A family gathered around a kitchen table discussing emergency plans, with papers, a map, and a notebook spread out
A hand-drawn neighborhood map showing two different evacuation routes marked with arrows and a meeting point marked with a star
A simple hand-drawn floor plan of a home showing rooms labeled, doors and windows marked, and two different escape routes drawn with colored arrows
A Scout reaching up to press the test button on a smoke detector mounted on a hallway ceiling
A family disaster kit laid out on a table showing water jugs, canned food, flashlights, batteries, first aid kit, weather radio, and important documents in a waterproof bag
A Scout and an adult walking through a kitchen with a clipboard checklist, the Scout pointing at a fire extinguisher mounted on the wall
Three panels showing nonswimming water rescue methods: reaching with a pole from a dock, throwing a ring buoy, and rowing a small boat toward a person in the water
Overhead view of large ground-to-air signal symbols (V, X, arrow) made from rocks and branches arranged on a sandy clearing in a forest opening
Two Scouts carefully carrying an improvised blanket-and-poles stretcher through a wooded trail, demonstrating proper carrying technique
Four Scouts working as a team to carry a stretcher along a narrow woodland trail, communicating and watching the path

An organizational chart showing the Incident Command System structure: Incident Commander at the top with Operations, Planning, Logistics, and Finance/Administration sections below, each with relevant icons
A personal emergency service go bag laid out on a table with all contents organized and visible: water bottle, food, first aid kit, flashlight, rain gear, gloves, notepad, and whistle
A career path infographic showing different emergency services careers (firefighter, EMT, emergency manager, dispatcher, HAZMAT technician) branching from a central Emergency Preparedness label
Teens wearing CERT green helmets and vests practicing light search and rescue techniques during a training exercise at a simulated disaster scene
